column1: # Written by Claude (origin "claude"). One line per entry:  entry id|typical learner mistake|usage note
# Notes are in English. Either text column may be empty.
es:ser:verb|Ser is for identity and lasting qualities ("soy médico", "es alta"), estar for states and where things are ("estoy cansado", "está en casa").|
es:estar:verb|Estar is for states and location ("estoy cansado", "Madrid está en España"); ser for identity and lasting qualities.|
es:éxito:noun|Means success. An exit is "salida".|
es:actualmente:adverb|Means currently, not actually. "Actually" is "en realidad".|
es:librería:noun|A librería is a bookshop. A library is "biblioteca".|
es:realizar:verb|Means to carry out, to achieve. To realize (notice) is "darse cuenta".|
es:asistir:verb|"Asistir a" means to attend. To help is ayudar.|
es:carpeta:noun|Means folder. A carpet is "alfombra".|
es:sensible:adjective|Means sensitive. "Sensible" in English is "sensato".|
es:recordar:verb|Means to remember or to remind. To record is "grabar".|
es:gustar:verb|Gustar works backwards: the thing you like is the subject. "Me gusta el café", "me gustan los perros".|
es:tener:verb||Age and many states use tener: "tengo 20 años", "tengo hambre", "tengo frío".
es:haber:verb||Hay means "there is / there are". Haber also makes the perfect: "he comido".
es:usted:pronoun||Usted is the polite "you", with the verb in the third person: "¿Cómo está usted?"
es:vosotros:pronoun||Vosotros is used only in Spain. In Latin America ustedes is the plural "you" for everyone.
es:coger:verb||In Spain coger means to take or catch. In much of Latin America (Mexico, Argentina) it is vulgar: use tomar or agarrar.
es:largo:adjective|Largo means long, not large (grande).|
es:ropa:noun|Ropa means clothes. A rope is "cuerda".|
es:pretender:verb|Pretender means to intend or aim, not to pretend (fingir).|
es:soportar:verb|Soportar means to put up with. To support is "apoyar".|
es:saber:verb|Saber is for facts and skills ("sé nadar"), conocer for people and places ("conozco Madrid").|
es:conocer:verb|Conocer is for people and places; for facts and skills use saber: "sé dónde vive".|
es:esperar:verb||Esperar means to wait, to hope and to expect.
es:muy:adverb|Muy goes before adjectives and adverbs (muy cansado, muy bien), mucho with nouns and verbs (mucho dinero, trabajo mucho).|
es:mucho:adverb|Mucho goes with verbs and nouns (trabajo mucho, mucho dinero); before adjectives use muy (muy grande).|
es:por:preposition|Por is for cause, route, exchange and duration ("gracias por todo", "por la calle"); para for purpose, destination and deadlines ("para ti", "para mañana").|
es:para:preposition|Para is for purpose, destination and deadlines ("es para ti", "para el lunes"); por for cause, route and exchange.|
es:quedar:verb||"Quedar con alguien" means to meet up with someone (Spain); "quedarse" means to stay.
es:molestar:verb|Molestar means to bother or annoy.|
